peabiru: multimodal routing on OpenStreetMap and GTFS networks

Source: R/peabiru-package.R
peabiru-package.Rd

peabiru builds a network from an 'OpenStreetMap' extract, 'GTFS' feeds and an optional elevation raster with build_network(), and computes, by walking, cycling, driving and public transport: travel-time matrices (travel_time_matrix(), expanded_travel_time_matrix(), arrival_travel_time_matrix()), accessibility (accessibility()), isochrones (isochrone()) and detailed itineraries (detailed_itineraries()), with or without fares (setup_fare_structure(), read_fare_structure(), write_fare_structure(), pareto_frontier()) and scenarios of car speeds and traffic stress. It inspects a network with find_snap(), street_network_bbox(), street_network_to_sf(), transit_network_to_sf(), check_transit_availability() and get_gtfs_errors(). The routing engine is written in 'Rust' and runs inside the R session; no 'Java' is needed. What the package does not support is an error that says so, never silently ignored.

Details

The routing engine is a 'Rust' port of Conveyal's 'R5' routing engine, and the functions are modelled on those of the 'r5r' package (Ipea), from whose 'Java' code the fare calculator and parts of the trip planner are translated; see the references, and the article "Compared with r5r" on the package website. peabiru is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Conveyal, Ipea or the r5r team.

Class of the results

The tables the functions return are tibbles by default. The option peabiru.output, read at each call, chooses another class:

  • options(peabiru.output = "tibble") (the default; 'tibble' is the package's one dependency): tibbles, and sf tibbles (class c("sf", "tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame")) for the results with a geometry, as sf::st_as_sf() makes of a tibble;

  • options(peabiru.output = "data.frame"): base data.frames, and plain sf data frames;

  • options(peabiru.output = "data.table") (needs 'data.table'): data.tables: sf data.tables for isochrone polygons, itineraries, the street edges and the transit routes, plain sf data frames for isochrone lines, street vertices and transit stops, and an index on the column found of find_snap(). A good choice for large matrices handled with 'data.table'.

Any other value is an error. The option applies to every table: the matrices, accessibility, Pareto frontiers, find_snap(), check_transit_availability(), get_gtfs_errors(), the tables of a fare structure, the tables of trip_options() and the sf results (whose geometries are always in EPSG:4326). The rows, the columns, their order and types, and the row names are the same whatever the class.

Sample data

system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru") holds a small network for examples and tests, cut from the Sao Paulo sample data of the r5r project: spo_osm.pbf, the streets around Avenida Paulista (data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright); spo_gtfs.zip, the SPTrans frequency-based 'GTFS' feed of that sample, without shapes.txt; and spo_points.csv, 27 points of its hexagonal grid with their population and opportunity counts.

References

Conway, M. W., Byrd, A. and van der Linden, M. (2017). Evidence-based transit and land use sketch planning using interactive accessibility methods on combined schedule and headway-based networks. Transportation Research Record, 2653(1), 45-53. doi:10.3141/2653-06

Conway, M. W., Byrd, A. and van Eggermond, M. (2018). Accounting for uncertainty and variation in accessibility metrics for public transport sketch planning. Journal of Transport and Land Use, 11(1). doi:10.5198/jtlu.2018.1074

Conway, M. W. and Stewart, A. F. (2019). Getting Charlie off the MTA: a multiobjective optimization method to account for cost constraints in public transit accessibility metrics. International Journal of Geographical Information Science, 33(9), 1759-1787. doi:10.1080/13658816.2019.1605075

Delling, D., Pajor, T. and Werneck, R. F. (2015). Round-based public transit routing. Transportation Science, 49(3), 591-604. doi:10.1287/trsc.2014.0534

Geisberger, R., Sanders, P., Schultes, D. and Vetter, C. (2012). Exact routing in large road networks using contraction hierarchies. Transportation Science, 46(3), 388-404. doi:10.1287/trsc.1110.0401

Pereira, R. H. M., Saraiva, M., Herszenhut, D., Braga, C. K. V. and Conway, M. W. (2021). r5r: Rapid Realistic Routing on Multimodal Transport Networks with R5 in R. Findings. doi:10.32866/001c.21262
